Consult Summary:
- 31-year-old woman with 2 months of worsening work-related anxiety causing insomnia, palpitations, low mood, and reduced social/physical activities; no suicidal ideation; plan for talking therapy self-referral, online resources, sleep advice, basic blood tests, and GP follow-up after labs.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Anxiety for ~2 months, primarily related to starting a new, stressful job in a fashion retailer head office; dread of going to work; significant worry about performance and interactions with supervisor.
- Timeline/progression: Onset ~2 months ago coinciding with new job; symptoms worsening over the past couple of months.
- Sleep: Difficulty initiating sleep (lying awake for hours), shallow sleep; wakes before alarm with racing heart; estimated 3–4 hours/night.
- Palpitations: Typically mornings when fearing being late or after oversleeping; described as irregular, lasting a few minutes up to ~10 minutes; once feared having a heart attack; chest pain denied initially but later described “painful when heart is beating fast” (conflict noted).
- Daytime function/mood: Very low energy; anhedonia (no enjoyment in usual activities including running/tennis and socializing); constant feeling down even on weekends; on edge; avoids some social activities but continues to attend work.
- Panic attacks: Denied; concerned symptoms may be building up toward one.
- Appetite: No significant change; increased chocolate intake when feeling down; eating regularly.
- Associated situations: Public transport (tube) feels stressful, worse with heat; majority of anxiety is work-focused.
- Past episodes: No prior similar episodes reported.
- Safety: Denies suicidal thoughts; has good family support.
- Self-help to date: Spoke with mother (who has past depression). No prior counseling or therapy.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions documented.
- No prior mental health diagnoses documented.
- Medications: None documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with parents.
- Occupation: Head office role at fashion retailer; started ~2 months ago; high stress; negative interactions with supervisor.
- Activities: Previously enjoyed running and tennis; currently reduced due to low enjoyment and fatigue.
- Alcohol: Drinks “quite a lot” on Fridays/Saturdays (reports exceeding limits on those days); occasional glass of wine during the week; exact quantities not documented.
- Tobacco: Occasional smoking.
- Recreational drugs: Denies use.

Family History:
- Mother with history of depression.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- Planned: “Basic blood tests” to evaluate palpitations; specifics not documented.
- No results available yet.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Work-related anxiety with insomnia, low energy, anhedonia; no suicidal ideation.
  - Plan:
    - Patient to self-refer to NHS talking therapy (Cognitive/behavioral-focused).
    - Provide online resources for anxiety management.
    - Provide advice on sleep patterns/sleep hygiene.
    - Safety-net: Call back if symptoms worsen, if unable to cope with work or daily activities.
    - Consider medication for anxiety if symptoms persist or worsen (not first-line per discussion).
- Issue 2: Palpitations, likely anxiety-related; described as irregular and episodic; no clear chest pain, conflicting report of “painful when fast.”
  - Plan:
    - Arrange basic blood tests; patient to call support line to schedule.
    - GP follow-up one week after blood tests to review results.
- General plan items:
  - Provide links/details for therapy self-referral and online resources.
  - Patient agreeable to one-to-one therapy.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Past medical/surgical history, allergies, full medication list/reconciliation, detailed alcohol units per week, detailed substance use, vitals, mental state exam, formal screening scores (e.g., GAD-7/PHQ-9), risk assessment (self-harm history, safeguarding), menstrual/OB-GYN history if relevant.
- Internal conflicts: Chest pain denied initially but later described palpitations as “painful when heart is beating fast” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Some segments were unclear/inaudible or truncated; exact quantities and certain details not captured.
